title: ALMA astrometry of the objects within 0.5 pc of Sagittarius A<SUP>*</SUP>
question: Whether ALMA can serve as a powerful tool for precision astrometry of compact objects and stars in the Nuclear Star Cluster within 0.5 pc of Sagittarius A* by measuring relative positions and proper motions.

data.sensitivity: 226 GHz continuum: 12 uJy/beam (NW), 15 uJy/beam (BW); H30a line: 110 uJy/beam per 20 km/s channel (NW); 230 GHz continuum: 39 uJy/beam (NW); 343 GHz continuum: 100 uJy/beam (BW), 80 uJy/beam (UW)

what.value: Infrared proper motions of stars in the Nuclear Star Cluster for comparison in Table 3 and text

evidence.loc: Proper Motion Referenced to Sgr A* of the Detected Objects in the Nuclear Star Cluster
evidence.quote: The proper motions by IR observations are also shown for comparison in Table 3 ((cite: Paumard), (cite: Muzic2008), (cite: Schodel2009)).

recipe.goal: Sub-select observation epochs to minimize time-variability artifacts of Sgr A* and perform iterative self-calibration and continuum/line imaging
recipe.method: Select first 7 days of Oct 2017 data and last 2 days of Jun 2019 data; perform iterative phase and amplitude self-calibration with gaincal, applycal, and tclean; subtract continuum with uvcontsub (fitorder=1) and image H30alpha line with tclean.
key_parameters: solint='inf' (first 2 self-cal iterations, phase only), solint='int' (successive iterations, then phase+amplitude), 7-8 iterations
natural weight and Briggs weight (robust parameter = 0.5)
assumptions: Sources in FOV are assumed non-variable during synthesis imaging

recipe.goal: Measure astrometric positions, peak flux densities, and angular sizes of Sgr A* and compact objects in the continuum maps
recipe.method: 2-D Gaussian fitting and deconvolution on the continuum maps at 343 GHz (2016.693), 226 GHz (2017.773, Briggs weight chosen for positions), and 230 GHz (2019.471, natural weight) using CASA task imfit.
key_parameters: Point source threshold: deconvolved size much smaller than synthesized beam (30 mas at 230 GHz, 40 mas at 226 GHz, 100 mas at 343 GHz)
assumptions: WR stars are assumed not to vary significantly in flux density within the elapsed time between 2017.773 and 2019.471

recipe.goal: Derive proper motions relative to Sgr A* and evaluate orbital kinematics
recipe.method: Subtract Sgr A* position from star positions at 2017.773 and 2019.471, compute angular shifts (Delta Ra, Delta Dec) over Delta t = 1.698 yr, convert to linear velocities at d = 8.0 kpc, and compare with Keplerian orbital velocity limits around Sgr A*.
assumptions: Galactic center distance d = 8.0 kpc; GCBH mass M_GCBH ~ 4 x 10^6 M_sun

recipe.goal: Measure radial velocities and line widths from H30alpha recombination line profiles
recipe.method: Extract H30alpha spectra toward compact objects and fit 1-D Gaussian profiles to determine central velocity and deconvolved FWHM velocity width.
key_parameters: Velocity channel width Delta V ~ 20 km s^-1; instrumental broadening correction sqrt(Delta V_obs^2 - (2*sampling)^2)

score_reason: All three ALMA project codes, CASA versions, weighting schemes, self-calibration iteration counts, solution intervals, and full source catalogs (positions, fluxes, proper motions for 65 objects) are explicitly provided, though low-level tclean parameters, exact execution block IDs for June 2019, and imfit box regions are omitted.
rediscovery_reason: All ALMA data are public in the archive with explicit project codes, the self-calibration and imfit astrometric workflow uses standard CASA tasks, and the main results are concrete numeric tables of positions, flux densities, and proper motions for 65 objects.
